vulnerabilities.description: Raptor RDF Syntax Library through 2.0.16: heap-based buffer over-read in the N-Triples parser when a bnode id ends in '.'

analysis.detail: The bundled raptor is built with --enable-parsers="rdfxml" only (engine/external/redland/ExternalProject_raptor.mk), so the vulnerable N-Triples parser is not compiled in. The upstream fix is additionally backported via engine/external/redland/raptor/raptor-backport-unreleased-fixes.patch.1.

vulnerabilities.description: Raptor RDF Syntax Library through 2.0.16: integer underflow when normalizing a URI in raptor_uri_normalize_path(), reported via the Turtle parser

analysis.detail: The upstream fix (return an empty buffer when the path length reaches 0) is backported via engine/external/redland/raptor/raptor-backport-unreleased-fixes.patch.1, and CVE-2024-57823.patch.1 additionally makes the path length sanity checks unconditional. The reported trigger, the Turtle parser, is not compiled in either (--enable-parsers="rdfxml").

vulnerabilities.description: Remote command execution in the 'curl' RUBY GEM <= 0.0.9

analysis.detail: Product name collision: this CVE is about the abandoned Ruby gem named 'curl', not the curl project. The bundled component is curl by the curl project (https://curl.se/).

vulnerabilities.description: graphite2: heap buffer overflow in lz4::decompress

analysis.detail: Fixed upstream in graphite2 1.3.10 (2017); the bundled 1.3.15 contains the fix. Flagged only because of a sloppy NVD version range.

vulnerabilities.description: Double free in OpenJPEG j2k_read_ppm_v3 as bundled by 2015-era PDFium/Chrome

analysis.detail: Fixed upstream in OpenJPEG r2997 (2015). The bundled PDFium is the 7988 snapshot (2026), which has contained the fix for a decade.

vulnerabilities.description: libtiff: segfault in TIFFReadRGBATileExt() (DoS)

analysis.detail: Fixed upstream in January 2024, first released in libtiff 4.7.0; the bundled 4.7.2 contains the fix.

vulnerabilities.description: libtiff: out-of-memory in TIFFOpen via a crafted file (DoS)

analysis.detail: Fixed upstream in November 2023, first released in libtiff 4.7.0; the bundled 4.7.2 contains the fix.

vulnerabilities.description: libxml2: integer overflow in xmlBuildQName() leading to a stack buffer overflow

analysis.detail: Fixed upstream in libxml2 2.13.8/2.14.2 (2025); the bundled 2.15.3 contains the fix.

vulnerabilities.description: libtiff: heap buffer overflow in the tiffcp utility

analysis.detail: Only the libtiff library is built and statically linked; the tiffcp command-line utility is neither built nor shipped.

vulnerabilities.description: libxml2: stack buffer overflow in the xmllint interactive shell

analysis.detail: Only the libxml2 library is shipped; the xmllint utility is neither built nor shipped.

vulnerabilities.description: libxml2: stack buffer overflows in the xmlcatalog utility --shell mode

analysis.detail: Only the libxml2 library is shipped; the xmlcatalog utility is neither built nor shipped.

vulnerabilities.description: FPE in pixman's 'stress-test' test utility

analysis.detail: The flaw is in pixman's stress-test test program, not in the library; the test programs are neither built nor shipped.

vulnerabilities.description: libxslt: use-after-free via attribute type corruption when processing result tree fragments

analysis.detail: The mitigation for this unfixed libxslt flaw lives in libxml2 >= 2.14 (per the Debian security tracker); the bundled libxml2 is 2.15.3, and libxslt only ever runs against it (both are statically linked together).

vulnerabilities.description: libxslt: use-after-free with key data stored cross-RVT

analysis.detail: The upstream fix (GNOME libxslt merge request !77, 'Use a dedicated node type to maintain the list of cached RVTs', the same commit RHEL backports for this CVE) is applied to the bundled 1.1.45 via engine/external/libxslt/77.patch.1.

vulnerabilities.description: Python: POP3 command injection via user-controlled commands in poplib

analysis.detail: Unlike the other Python findings, shipped product code uses this module: program/mailmerge.py imports poplib. Fixed upstream only in 3.15.0a6. To assess: whether the mail-merge POP3 path is reachable at all in Collabora Online (a headless server; mail merge account configuration is a desktop feature) and whether the injected commands cross a trust boundary given the server configuration is user-supplied to begin with.

vulnerabilities.description: cairo through 1.18.4: assertion failure in _cairo_ft_unscaled_font_fini (DoS)

analysis.detail: No upstream fix yet. Impact is an assertion-failure crash; reported via Poppler's usage. To assess: whether the reported sequence is reachable through vcl's cairo usage and whether release builds compile the assertion out.

vulnerabilities.description: libtiff: signed integer overflow in putcontig8bitYCbCr44tile leading to heap overflow in YCbCr tile decoding

analysis.detail: The bundled tiff-4.7.2 tarball already contains the upstream fix (libtiff commit 782a11d6, 'prevent integer overflow ... in YCbCr tile decoding functions'): all four affected 'incr' computations are the fixed const tmsize_t form. Verified in the tarball source; the advisory's version range is inaccurate.
